description: Use SIMD instructions (AVX2/SSE) to accelerate the copying of literal byte runs and LZ77 back-references during DEFLATE decompression. While Huffman decoding is latency-bound, the LZ77 reconstruction phase can be throughput-bound on memory bandwidth. Vectorized 16/32-byte copies with overlapping writes can dramatically speed up literal runs.
mathematical_formalization: For a literal run of length L bytes: scalar_cycles = L * c_store, simd_cycles = ceil(L/W) * c_vstore where W=16 (SSE) or 32 (AVX2). Speedup = L * c_store / (ceil(L/W) * c_vstore). For back-refs with distance d >= W, same formula applies. For d < W, need overlapping copy: cycles = ceil(L/d) * c_vstore.
analogical_connections: Flood fill in graphics: filling large contiguous regions with a single operation
Broadcast in network protocols: one message replicated to many destinations
Gene duplication in biology: copying segments efficiently
implementation_hypothesis: Implement chunkcopy_simd(): for each LZ77 token, determine if distance >= 16. If so, use SSE movdqu to copy 16 bytes at a time, allowing overlap past the end. For short distances (1-15), use SSSE3 pshufb to create a repeating pattern.
experiment_seed: Benchmark LZ77 reconstruction with scalar vs SSE vs AVX2 copies on files with different literal/match ratios. Measure throughput in GB/s for the copy phase alone.
